svg.title: Part families – rank order clustering
svg.text: 02 – Group technology: machine–part matrix before and after rank order clustering (ROC, King 1980)
1 = the part needs this machine. ROC sorts rows and columns by their binary weight until nothing changes (2 passes here). Blocks = machine cells + part families.
Before: rows and columns in arbitrary order
After ROC: 3 cells / families on the diagonal
Cell A – prismatic housings: M6 Washer + M1 HMC → P1 crankcase, P4 cylinder head
Cell B – bores and flat faces: M2 VMC + M3 Hone + M7 Lapping → P2 cylinder, P5 valve plate, P8 conrod
Cell C – rotational parts: M4 Lathe + M5 cyl. grinder → P6 pulley, P3 crankshaft, P7 bearing cover
Exceptional elements (red circles) = 3: P2 and P5 need the washer of cell A; P6 needs the VMC for its keyway.
Fix: washer as a shared central resource (taken out of the matrix) + lathe with driven tools for the keyway → 0 exceptions.
after the fixes: e = 14, e_out = 0, e_void = 3
